def first_name_amount_over_25(lines):
    """Identify, within a single buffer snapshot from the request-logging
    service, the earliest record whose reported amount has crossed the
    alerting threshold.

    Background. The ingestion tier of the logging service emits, for every
    upstream response it processes, a compact three-field record; the
    aggregation daemon appends these records to an in-memory buffer in
    arrival order. During a recent incident review it became necessary to
    determine, for a given snapshot of that buffer, which record was the
    first to exceed the amount threshold of 25 that the on-call rotation
    uses to flag anomalous responses. This function performs exactly that
    determination and is invoked by the incident-summary generator.

    Input. The parameter lines represents one buffer snapshot, presented
    in the order in which the records were appended by the daemon; no
    re-sorting has been applied upstream. Each element of lines is a list
    of exactly three values: a tag (str), a amount (int), and a weight
    (int). In production, the tag is ordinarily the short name of the
    handler that produced the response, although the literal string
    'error' appears whenever the originating handler could not be
    identified by the collector. The amount is the figure extracted from
    the response payload, and the weight is a routing annotation recorded
    by the load balancer for its own separate bookkeeping.

    Output. Return the tag of the FIRST entry (in the given order) whose
    amount is strictly greater than 25, or None if no entry qualifies.
    The value produced here is copied verbatim into the first-offender
    field of the generated incident summary, which is why the original
    ordering of the snapshot is significant to the reviewers. An empty
    snapshot is a legitimate occurrence in this pipeline — it arises
    whenever the buffer was flushed between two consecutive polling
    intervals — and it corresponds to the case in which no entry
    qualifies.

    Examples:

    >>> first_name_amount_over_25([['Bo', 38, 8], ['Bo', 35, 14], ['Dee', 29, 24], ['Cy', 30, 6], ['Dee', 39, 9], ['error', 17, 10]])
    'Bo'
    >>> first_name_amount_over_25([['error', 30, 29], ['widget', 17, 23], ['error', 14, 15], ['Cy', 37, 20], ['Bo', 12, 21], ['Bo', 25, 14], ['error', 29, 16]])
    'error'
    >>> first_name_amount_over_25([])
    """
